questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Element-Atomic number)List-II (Position in periodic table)
(a)Ra – 88(i)$4^{th}$ period, $13^{th}$ group
(b)Ga – 31(ii)$6^{th}$ period, $6^{th}$ group
(c)W – 74(iii)$5^{th}$ period, $10^{th}$ group
(d)Pd – 46(iv)$7^{th}$ period, $2^{nd}$ group
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
The position of an element in the periodic table can be determined using its atomic number and the nearest preceding noble gas.

(a) Ra ($Z = 88$): The preceding noble gas is Radon (Rn, $Z = 86$), which belongs to the $6^{th}$ period and $18^{th}$ group. The next two electrons enter the $7s$ orbital. Thus, Ra belongs to the $7^{th}$ period and $2^{nd}$ group. (a) → (iv)

(b) Ga ($Z = 31$): The preceding noble gas is Argon (Ar, $Z = 18$), which belongs to the $3^{rd}$ period. The next electrons fill the $4s$, $3d$, and $4p$ orbitals. The group number is $31 - 18 = 13$. Thus, Ga belongs to the $4^{th}$ period and $13^{th}$ group. (b) → (i)

(c) W ($Z = 74$): The preceding noble gas is Xenon (Xe, $Z = 54$), which belongs to the $5^{th}$ period. The next electrons fill the $6s$, $4f$ (14 elements), and $5d$ orbitals. The group number is $74 - 54 - 14 = 6$. Thus, W belongs to the $6^{th}$ period and $6^{th}$ group. (c) → (ii)

(d) Pd ($Z = 46$): The preceding noble gas is Krypton (Kr, $Z = 36$), which belongs to the $4^{th}$ period. The next electrons fill the $5s$ and $4d$ orbitals. The group number is $46 - 36 = 10$. Thus, Pd belongs to the $5^{th}$ period and $10^{th}$ group. (d) → (iii)

The correct matching is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

Answer: a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d–iii

questions.q: Silicon doped with gallium forms
questions.solution: Silicon belongs to group 14 and gallium comes in group 13. So, when Si is doped with Ga, $p$-type of semiconductor is produced as group 13 elements have only 3 valence electrons, there on combination with group 14 elements produce an electron deficient bond or have electron vacancy and as such can move through the crystal like a positive charge giving rise to electrical conductivity.

The size of anion is always higher than that of the parentatom due to the decrease in effective nuclear charge on anion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Malleability and ductility of metals can be accounted due to
options: the capacity of layers of metal ions to slide over the other
the interaction of electrons with metal ions in the lattice
questions.solution: In metallic bonds, the valence shell electrons are delocalised and shared between many atoms. These delocalised electrons allow the metal atoms to slide past one another without being subjected to strong repulsive forces. The malleability and ductility of metals is due to this sliding capacity of the delocalised electrons.
